input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I found no evidence that would weaken or overturn the conclusion that hosting and data center costs were the main reason for the increase in Adobe's cost of subscription revenue in Q3 FY2026.

H1 (One-time charges): The retrieved evidence (E7, E8, E9) does not mention any one-time charges, restructuring costs, or unusual items affecting subscription costs in Q3 FY2026. The cost breakdown in E3 shows "Various individually insignificant items" contributing only 2% to the total 24% change, which does not suggest material one-time impacts.

H2 (Acquisitions impact): While E11 mentions the acquisition of Semrush in April 2026, this is discussed in the context of revenue enhancement for Adobe Experience Manager offerings, not in relation to cost of subscription revenue. The evidence does not indicate that this acquisition distorted the cost comparison or affected the attribution of hosting and data center costs as the main driver.

H3 (Accounting changes): The retrieved evidence (E13, E14, E15) shows consistent definitions and descriptions of cost of subscription revenue components across periods, with no mention of changes in cost allocation methodology or accounting treatment that would make the year-over-year comparison misleading.

The original supporting evidence remains valid: E3 explicitly states that cost of subscription revenue increased "primarily due to" hosting services and data center costs contributing 22 percentage points out of a total 24% increase in Q3 FY2026. This represents over 90% of the total increase, clearly establishing hosting and data center costs as the main driver. E6 confirms the 24% increase in subscription costs ($633M vs $510M) for the three months ended August 28, 2026.
